A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: Sections 3 and 6 and Appendix E report original numerical experiments on regret-matching algorithms, including benchmark games and 25 random matrix games.

after.justification: Sections 3 and 6 and Appendices C and H report original convergence experiments, including additional trajectory, baseline, and best-iterate results.

M1.justification: The ExRM+, SPRM+, and restarted algorithms retain their update rules, projections, and restart criteria. The new alternating PRM+ pseudocode documents a variant already evaluated in v1; EG and OG are added comparators.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 3-by-3 game, normal-form Kuhn poker and Goofspiel, and Gaussian random games of size 10-by-15. The additional diagnostics reuse this coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 3 retains the six RM-family algorithms and adds extragradient (EG) and optimistic gradient descent (OG), also included in Figure 9. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparisons beyond regret-matching methods.

E3.justification: Section 6 replaces v1's fixed stepsize of 0.1 with selection of the best stepsize from {1, 0.1, 0.01, 0.001, 0.0001}. v2 also introduces best-iterate evaluation and trajectory diagnostics using the final 2,000 of 100,000 iterations. Restart experiments retain stepsize 0.05.

E4.justification: v2 adds strategy-trajectory analyses of three nonconvergent variants in Appendix C and best-iterate convergence comparisons against a 1/sqrt(T) reference in Appendix H.4. Appendix H.3 adds a restart-rate analysis on the hard instance and an individual random game. These substantially extend the existing convergence diagnostics.

E5.justification: Both versions average results over 25 random matrix games and display confidence intervals. v2 adds no seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence-level specification, or statistical testing procedure.

E6.justification: v2 adds EG/OG results, including EG reaching the displayed 10^-10 floor on Goofspiel and OG performing comparatively slowly on random games. Figures 4-6, 8, and 9 add trajectory, restart-acceleration, and best-iterate findings. The revised main comparison uses different stepsize selection, so its curves do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: v2 adds supporting proofs of non-Lipschitzness and operator monotonicity properties, including a nonmonotonicity counterexample, and an explicit duality-gap convergence argument. Appendix E corrects Claim 1 to bound differences using normalized points g(z) and g(z'). The principal convergence rates and proof strategy remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The main asymptotic, best-iterate, and restarted linear-convergence claims remain. v2 extends the introductory negative empirical claim to best-iterate convergence and corrects contribution 4's reference to potentially nonconvergent SPRM+ to PRM+.

C2.justification: v2 explains why vanishing duality gaps and successive movements need not imply convergence to one point. It also distinguishes ExRM+'s lack of adversarial no-regret guarantees from SPRM+ and explicitly identifies extension through CFR to extensive-form games as unresolved.

D1.justification: Appendices A and H add explicit alternating PRM+, EG, and OG pseudocode. Appendix H.2 newly discloses Python 3.8.8, a 2.2 GHz Intel Core i7 laptop with 8 GB RAM, and approximate runtime of a few hours; these are disclosures, not established changes in computing resources.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kinderlehrer and Stampacchia (2000) and removes Hart and Mas-Colell (2000). It explicitly acknowledges that Theorem 1's proof largely follows Meng et al. (2023), previously described mainly as addressing an incomparable setting, and clarifies the dependence on classical variational-inequality analysis.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten. Section 4 separates duality-gap convergence from iterate convergence and brings the existing full uniqueness proof into the main text. Alternating variants move to an appendix, and the appendices are reorganized with a contents list and acknowledgements added.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR layout, resizes and relocates existing displays, expands Figure 3's legend and curves, and adds trajectory Figures 4-6, semilog Figure 8, and best-iterate Figure 9. v1's restart Figure 4 becomes Figure 7; several retained plots receive a 10^-10 display floor.

improvement.justification: v2 improves technical clarity through the corrected normalization bound, supporting operator proofs, and clearer attribution. Added gradient baselines and convergence diagnostics better substantiate the retained theoretical contribution. The gains are limited by underspecified selection of the 'best' stepsizes and Figure 8's inconsistency with the stated universal plotting floor.
